# NCR5386 - NCR 5386 SCSI protocol controller

Package DIP-48 · family MOS LSI · catalogue file [catalog/chips/NCR5386.json](https://github.com/RetroCoreLabs/RetroSchematic/blob/master/src/catalog/chips/NCR5386.json)

## Pins

| Pin | Name | Role | Active | Output type | Details |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | D2 | output |  | three-state | microprocessor data bus bit 2, active high, bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 2 | D1 | output |  | three-state | microprocessor data bus bit 1, active high, bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 3 | D0 | output |  | three-state | microprocessor data bus bit 0, active high, bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 4 | RESET | input | high |  | high forces the chip into reset: current operations end, internal storage is cleared and self-diagnostics run |
| 5 | ATN | output |  | three-state | INITIATOR ROLE: asserted when the microprocessor asks for attention or a received byte has a parity error. TARGET ROLE: input showing the SCSI ATN signal. bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 6 | IGS | output | high | totem-pole | initiator group select: high when the chip works as initiator; enables the external ATN and ACK drivers |
| 7 | I_O | output |  | three-state | I/O. INITIATOR ROLE: input showing the bus phase. TARGET ROLE: driven to show the bus phase. bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 8 | C_D | output |  | three-state | C/D. INITIATOR ROLE: input showing the bus phase. TARGET ROLE: driven to show the bus phase. bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 9 | MSG | output |  | three-state | INITIATOR ROLE: input showing the bus phase. TARGET ROLE: driven to show the bus phase. bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 10 | ACK | output |  | three-state | INITIATOR ROLE: asserted in answer to REQ for a byte transfer. TARGET ROLE: input answering REQ. bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 11 | REQ | output |  | three-state | INITIATOR ROLE: input: the target asks for a byte transfer. TARGET ROLE: asserted to ask for a byte transfer. bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 12 | /ID2 | input | low |  | SCSI ID bit 2 of the chip, active low; pull-up needed only when wired to a switch or strap |
| 13 | /ID1 | input | low |  | SCSI ID bit 1, active low |
| 14 | /ID0 | input | low |  | SCSI ID bit 0, active low. On the 5386 in pass-parity mode this pin is the data bus parity DP and pins 12-13 are unused (NCR SCSI Engineering Notebook) |
| 15 | ARB | output | high | totem-pole | arbitration phase: high lets external circuits put the ID bit on the SCSI bus |
| 16 | CLK | clock |  |  | symmetrical square wave that makes the internal timing; at most 10 MHz |
| 17 | BSYIN | input | high |  | high tells the chip the SCSI BSY signal is active |
| 18 | SELIN | input | high |  | high tells the chip the SCSI SEL signal is active |
| 19 | INT | output | high | totem-pole | interrupt to the microprocessor; set high on a request, cleared by reset or by reading the Interrupt Register |
| 20 | /SBEN | output | low | totem-pole | SCSI data bus enable: low enables the external SCSI data bus drivers |
| 21 | /CS | input | low |  | chip select: enables reading or writing the selected internal register; never active together with DACK |
| 22 | A0 | input |  |  | register address bit 0 (with CS) |
| 23 | A1 | input |  |  | register address bit 1 |
| 24 | GND | ground |  |  |  |
| 25 | A2 | input |  |  | register address bit 2 |
| 26 | A3 | input |  |  | register address bit 3 |
| 27 | /DACK | input | low |  | data acknowledge: resets DREQ and selects the Data Register (the chip select for DMA transfers) |
| 28 | TGS | output | high | totem-pole | target group select: high when the chip works as target; enables the external REQ, MSG, C/D and I/O drivers |
| 29 | DREQ | output | high | totem-pole | data request in DMA mode: high when the Data Register has a byte for, or needs a byte from, the DMA; cleared by DACK |
| 30 | /WR | input | low |  | write pulse: strobes the data bus into the selected internal register |
| 31 | /RD | input | low |  | read pulse: puts the selected internal register on the data bus |
| 32 | SELOUT | output | high | totem-pole | high while the chip asserts SEL on the SCSI bus |
| 33 | SBP | output |  | three-state | SCSI data bus parity, active high, to the external transceivers; bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 34 | SB0 | output |  | three-state | SCSI data bus bit 0, active high, to the external SCSI bus transceivers; bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 35 | SB1 | output |  | three-state | SCSI data bus bit 1, active high, to the external SCSI bus transceivers; bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 36 | SB2 | output |  | three-state | SCSI data bus bit 2, active high, to the external SCSI bus transceivers; bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 37 | SB3 | output |  | three-state | SCSI data bus bit 3, active high, to the external SCSI bus transceivers; bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 38 | SB4 | output |  | three-state | SCSI data bus bit 4, active high, to the external SCSI bus transceivers; bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 39 | SB5 | output |  | three-state | SCSI data bus bit 5, active high, to the external SCSI bus transceivers; bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 40 | SB6 | output |  | three-state | SCSI data bus bit 6, active high, to the external SCSI bus transceivers; bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 41 | SB7 | output |  | three-state | SCSI data bus bit 7, active high, to the external SCSI bus transceivers; bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 42 | BSYOUT | output | high | totem-pole | high while the chip asserts BSY on the SCSI bus |
| 43 | D7 | output |  | three-state | microprocessor data bus bit 7, active high, bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 44 | D6 | output |  | three-state | microprocessor data bus bit 6, active high, bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 45 | D5 | output |  | three-state | microprocessor data bus bit 5, active high, bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 46 | D4 | output |  | three-state | microprocessor data bus bit 4, active high, bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 47 | D3 | output |  | three-state | microprocessor data bus bit 3, active high, bidirectional (the 5385E data sheet gives no output type; shown as three-state) |
| 48 | VCC | power |  |  | +5 V |

## Sources

- [NCR Microelectronics Division SCSI Engineering Notebook, Rev. 2, October 1985](https://bitsavers.org/components/ncr_symbios/scsi/NCR_SCSI_Engineering_Notebook_Rev2_Oct85.pdf) - 41 (NCR 5386 48-pin DIP pinout); 4-5 (differences from the 5385E: pin and software compatible superset, pass-parity on pin 14)
- [NCR 5385E SCSI Protocol Controller Data Sheet, May 1985](https://bitsavers.org/components/ncr_symbios/scsi/5385/NCR_5385E_SCSI_Protocol_Controller_Data_Sheet_May85.pdf) - 5-7 (pin description); NCR 5385E - the notebook states the 5386 is pin compatible with it; pin names and numbers checked against the 5386 pinout

No sheet in this repository uses this chip yet.
